title: The Ledger
logline: A village shop's handwritten credit book holds decades of small debts, some paid next week, some after the harvest, some quietly struck through when the debtor dies.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: What a community gives one of its own becomes what is owed on paper: a village shop's credit book, where some debts are struck through when the debtor dies.

thread_out.thread: The question of whether everything owed comes due moves from a ledger to a paddy field, where the rain that should keep coming simply stops.

requirements: A working village shop with a handwritten credit system and a shopkeeper willing to be filmed
Customers willing to be filmed at the counter, or filming arranged to protect their privacy

suggestions.name: A tea-estate village shop in the Nuwara Eliya or Uda Pussellawa area
suggestions.why: Small rural shops with long-running credit books are still common in tea-growing hill country.
